subject: EU / APAC private-deploy residency: handoff, network & authorization
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmegrid.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmegrid.com <procurement@acmegrid.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Residency handoff and network zones for EU/APAC private deploy

Diego,

Thanks for the call earlier. We need a short, auditable handoff plan that explains how Redwood will ensure EU data residency while providing warm-standby failover to APAC for disaster scenarios. Key asks from our side:

- Confirmation that customer data at rest for EU tenants remains within EU physical regions (control plane exceptions documented).
- Network topology for failover (peering, transit, private interconnect) and how we prevent cross-border egress during steady-state routing changes.
- KMS/Key custody approach and whether keys remain in customer-managed KMS in EU.
- Expected cutover window and rollback criteria for a failover.
- Evidence artifacts we can include in our audit (network diagrams, runbook snippets, signed authorization).

Can you share a short plan and confirm the attachments you can provide? Procurement also wants to know if there are any material SLA exceptions for warm-standby.

Sanjay Patel
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Grid Utilities
On behalf of Acme procurement team

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmegrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@acmegrid.com <procurement@acmegrid.com>
Date: 2028-12-02T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency handoff and network zones for EU/APAC private deploy

Sanjay — thanks, this is clear and actionable. High level response + will attach a concise handoff packet. Quick summary below; full packet attached (redwood-residency-handoff-v1.pdf) and network diagram (network-diagram-v2.svg).

1) Data residency (steady state):
- Customer data-at-rest (models, KV caches, logs identified in our tenancy config) will be provisioned on EU-only storage/volumes pinned to the agreed EU region. Control plane metadata used for orchestration will have a documented exception scope and is accessible to the customer via audit logs.

2) Failover topology (warm standby in APAC):
- Primary compute and storage remain in EU. We provision a warm-standby cluster in APAC with no active write replication for EU-resident storage. During a failover, we follow an authorization workflow (signed runbook steps) that documents explicit approval from an authorised Acme operator; only then do we enable cross-region replication modes.
- Network: traffic routing uses private peering and a pre-approved transit path. Border egress controls are enforced by route filters and ingress ACLs to prevent inadvertent EU egress.

3) KMS / keys:
- We recommend customer-managed KMS with keys hosted in EU. Redwood supports both customer KMS (recommended) and Redwood-managed KMS with strict key residency options. If the customer brings EU KMS, we keep all key operations local to EU unless a documented emergency key-rotation/replication is authorized.

4) Cutover and rollback:
- Cutover is executed in stages (canary / regional gate / full switch). Rollback criteria are defined (latency degradation, error ratio above threshold, failed integrity checks). The process is reversible within the maintenance window; we provide automated rollback hooks.

5) Evidence package:
- Attachments include network diagram, excerpted runbook with approval steps and a signed authorization template you can use in DocuSign.

SLA implications: warm-standby activation is covered by the Dedicated contract variant but will have a 4–8 hour RTO for full service restoration unless you opt for higher reserved standby capacity (we can quote). I'll loop in our sales/engr team for exact numbers.

Attaching: redwood-residency-handoff-v1.pdf, network-diagram-v2.svg

— Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmegrid.com>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-04T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency handoff and network zones for EU/APAC private deploy

Hi Sanjay — adding operational detail and acceptance checkpoints.

Operational guards we will commit to in the handoff packet:
- Pre-approved authorization list (names + roles) who can initiate cross-region replication. We will only proceed on a ramp that requires 2-step authorization (customer + Redwood on-call).
- Read-only verification window: when failover is staged, reads may be allowed from APAC but writes are gated until the final approval; we will log every access event and provide a signed event bundle for audit.
- Network ACL snapshot: we will capture and provide a time-bound network ACL and route snapshot right before and after the change.

Can you confirm the list of individuals from Acme who can sign for the authorization? Also, is Acme comfortable with the read-gated approach (reads allowed early, writes gated)?

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmegrid.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmegrid.com <procurement@acmegrid.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-05T10:11:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency handoff and network zones for EU/APAC private deploy

Thanks Marissa — Acme confirms two authorized approvers: myself (Sanjay Patel) and Priya Desai (Head of Ops) — both will be on the DocuSign authorization. We are fine with read-gated early access provided we get the event bundle and ACL snapshots you mentioned. Procurement asks for a short note on cost impact of keeping warm-standby idle vs. burst-ready.

Procurement note: any line-item for standby-reservation should be in a separate annex so we can approve the core private-deploy SOW without committing to premium standby pricing.

Sanjay

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmegrid.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, procurement@acmegrid.com <procurement@acmegrid.com>
Date: 2028-12-09T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency handoff and network zones for EU/APAC private deploy

Folks — next steps and timeline to get this into Acme's audit package: 

1) Deliverables by 2028-12-12: finalized handoff packet (attached PDF updated), network diagram SVG, and a short runbook excerpt (included in PDF).
2) DocuSign authorization template ready for signers (Sanjay + Priya). We'll not trigger any cross-region change until both signatures are present.
3) Quote: separate annex for standby-reservation pricing; procurement will get a draft by 2028-12-13 (Jordan will own).
4) Canaries and dry-run: propose a non-customer-affecting dry-run on 2028-12-20 (EU maintenance window) to capture ACL snapshots and the event bundle — this will be read-only verification. Please confirm availability.

Jordan — can you produce the annex and the pricing delta for idle warm-standby vs burst-ready? Karthik — please provide a one-page KMS options sheet (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed with residency guarantees).

Once we have signatures and the annex agreed, we'll add the final artifacts to your audit folder. Attaching v1 of the packet now; will push v2 with the annex once Jordan confirms pricing.

Thanks — Diego
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
